classification.difficultyReason: Same as p34-q5, but the angles are given as inclinations (130°, 215°, 320°) so students compute each reference angle before assigning quadrant signs.

content.prompt:
The points $A,B,C$ are on the unit circle. $O$ is the origin.
Find the coordinates of $A,B,C$.
Leave your answer in terms of $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the acute reference angle.

answer.worked:
On the unit circle, the coordinate magnitudes are $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the acute reference angle. Use the quadrant to determine their signs.

$A$ is in Q2, $B$ is in Q3 and $C$ is in Q4.

$$\begin{align*}\theta_A&=180^{\circ}-130^{\circ}=50^{\circ}\\\theta_B&=215^{\circ}-180^{\circ}=35^{\circ}\\\theta_C&=360^{\circ}-320^{\circ}=40^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}A&=(-\cos50^{\circ},\sin50^{\circ})\\B&=(-\cos35^{\circ},-\sin35^{\circ})\\C&=(\cos40^{\circ},-\sin40^{\circ}).\end{align*}$$
